sentences.text:
Dinesh Kumar And 2 Ors. vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21
March, 2023

Author: Shekhar Kumar Yadav
Bench: Shekhar Kumar Yadav
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 70
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 26937 of 2013
Applicant :- Dinesh Kumar And 2 Ors.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Vijay Kumar Dwivedi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate,Aditya Prasad Mishra
Hon'ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav,J.

This is a application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing the charge sheet no. 119A/2008 dated 7.7.2008 as well as entire Criminal proceeding of the Case no. 369 of 2008, (State Vs. Dinesh Kumar & others), arising out of Case Crime No. 172A of 2008, under Sections 323, 504, 506 IPC, P.S.
Uttaraon, District Allahabad, pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate 4th,
Allahabad.

It is contended by learned counsel for the applicants that the matter was referred to the mediation centre of this Court vide order dated 15.2.2023 to enable them to explore the possibility of compromise.
In pursuance thereto, the parties appeared before the Mediation and Conciliation Centre and settlement has been arrived at between the parties vide report of mediation centre dated 21.2.2023.
Both the counsel made a statement on behalf of the parties that the matter has been successfully sorted out.

They have also agreed that they will have no dispute with each other and all Dinesh Kumar And 2 Ors. vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111358438/
1 the cases filed by them against each other shall be withdrawn by the parties concerned by taking appropriate steps before the Court concerned.

entities.text: Dinesh Kumar And 2 Ors. vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since both the parties have amicably compromised the matter and no useful purpose would be served by continuing the the criminal proceedings.

The Apex Court in the case of B. S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana & others reported in 2003 (46) ACC Page 779 (S.C.), it is held that High Court is empowered to quash criminal proceedings of FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent powers, in case the parties have arrived at settlement agreement of their matrimonial disputes, and section 320 Cr.P.C does not limit or affect the powers under section 482 Cr.P.C.

entities.text: B. S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana & others reported in 2003 (46) ACC Page 779 (S.C.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The aforesaid case has also been relied in the case of Ruchi Agarwal Vs.
Amit Kumar Agarwal & others 2005 (51) ACC Page 217, where the Apex Court quashed the proceedings of criminal case under sections 498A, 323, 506 IPC read with section Dowry Prohibition Act as the parties have entered into a compromise.

entities.text:
Ruchi Agarwal Vs.
Amit Kumar Agarwal & others 2005 (51) ACC Page 217
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court in exercise of its inherent powers under section 482 Cr.P.C can quash the proceedings, where the parties have entered into compromise.

The Apex Court in the case of 'Madan Mohan Abbot v. State of Punjab' reported as (2008)4 SCC 582 emphasised in para No. 6 as follows:-
"6.

entities.text: Madan Mohan Abbot v. State of Punjab' reported as (2008)4 SCC 582
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We need to emphasize that it is perhaps advisable that in disputes where the question involved is of a purely personal nature, the Court should ordinarily accept the terms of the compromise even in criminal proceedings as keeping the matter alive with no possibility of a result in favour of the prosecution is a luxury which the Courts, grossly overburdened as they are, cannot afford and that the time so saved can be utilised in deciding more effective and meaningful litigation.
This is a common sense approach to the matter based on ground of realities and bereft of the technicalities of the law."

Taking into account the allegations and the fact that the compromise arrived at between the parties before the Mediation and Conciliation Centre of this Court there is no impediment in the way of this Court to quash the proceedings arising out of the same in view of the above said settled proposition of law.
Accordingly, the present petition is allowed.

The proceedings arising out of criminal Case No. 369 of 2008 (State Vs Dinesh Kumar and others) in Case Crime No. 172A of 2008,under Sections 323, 504,
506 IPC P.S. Uttraon, District Allahabad are hereby quashed.
